title: HPC for AI - Part 1
text:
Learning outcomes
By the end of this course, you will:

Understand when and why AI projects need high-performance computing (HPC).
Be able to start a JupyterHub session with GPUs on Isambard-AI.
Be able to prepare an image dataset and train an image classification model on a GPU.
Know how to judge a classifier on imbalanced medical data.
Understand how training a model on multiple GPUs works.
Know how to work considerately on a shared supercomputer.

title: Training on one GPU
text: Can a computer learn to spot a fracture?

title: Training on one GPU
text:
The model
We’ll use YOLOv8n-cls, a small image classifier. Training one from scratch needs far more than 4,000 images, so we use transfer learning: start from a model that has seen over a million everyday photos, then fine-tune it on X-rays.






Going deeper: why does transfer learning work on X-rays?





Early layers learn general features such as edges and textures. Fine-tuning mostly adjusts the later layers, so far fewer examples are needed.
